product_backlog.title: To-Do List Management
product_backlog.description: Manage creation and deletion of to-do lists.
Manage tasks within to-do lists, including addition, completion, and deletion.
product_backlog.title: Task Management
Web User Interface
product_backlog.description: Provide a clean, user-friendly web interface to view and manage lists and tasks.
As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Allows users to initiate organization by creating named to-do lists.
product_backlog.title: Create To-Do List
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the main application page, When the user enters a name for a new to-do list and clicks 'Create List', Then a new to-do list is created and displayed in the user's lists view.
Given the user is viewing a specific to-do list, When the user enters a task description and clicks 'Add Task', Then the task is added to the list and displayed.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can keep track of what needs to be done.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Enables users to record actionable items within their lists.
product_backlog.title: Add Task to List

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Allows users to track progress on individual items.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.
product_backlog.title: Mark Task Complete or Incomplete
acceptance_criteria: Given the user has tasks in a list, When the user clicks the complete/incomplete toggle for a task, Then the task status updates and is visually distinguished as complete or incomplete.

product_backlog.title: Delete Task
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove items I no longer need.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Keeps lists clean by removing obsolete tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user has tasks in a list, When the user clicks the delete button on a task, Then the task is removed from the list.

product_backlog.title: Delete Entire List
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Allows users to remove entire obsolete list structures.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user has an existing to-do list, When the user clicks the delete list button, Then the entire list and all its associated tasks are permanently removed.
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can clean up unneeded lists.

product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Provides comprehensive visibility into all todo items and lists.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user has multiple lists and tasks, When the user views the main application page, Then all lists and their respective tasks are displayed with completed tasks visually distinguished.
product_backlog.title: View Lists and Tasks Dashboard
product_backlog.description: As a user, I want to see all my lists and their tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished so that I have a clear overview.

The product vision for this entire evaluation, verbatim, is:

# Fixed Evaluation Scenario: To-Do List Web App

> **Do not edit this file to "make the eval easier" or to match whatever the team
> produced.** Its entire value is being byte-identical across runs, so results are
> comparable across Horseless Carriage versions over time. If the scenario itself
> needs to change, that's a deliberate decision with its own commit message
> explaining why — never a silent drift.

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.


Treat the sprint goal and backlog for this sprint as pre-approved by me (the human) - do not wait for further approval messages, proceed directly through planning, development, PR creation, CI verification, sprint review (create_sprint_report), and the release PR (create_release_pr) for this sprint's increment. Do not ask me anything else during this sprint - make reasonable decisions yourself and note them as assumptions in the sprint report.
